html:
The Hul'qumi'num Treaty Group stands on the map for the lands of the Hul'qumi'num-speaking peoples of southeast Vancouver Island and the nearby Gulf Islands, around Duncan, Chemainus and Ladysmith in British Columbia. They are part of the Coast Salish world.

These peoples, among them the Cowichan, Chemainus, Penelakut, Halalt and Lyackson, lived in cedar plank house villages and fished for salmon on the rivers and the Fraser. Most of their land was taken by settlers and the Esquimalt and Nanaimo Railway grant in the 1880s, with no treaty.

The Treaty Group was founded in 1993 to negotiate a treaty with British Columbia and Canada. It is based in Duncan and has reached the fifth of the six stages of the BC treaty process. Their neighbours to the west are the Ditidaht.
